winner.hypothesis: Replace 6 read Caffeine caches (vertexById, verticesByLabel, neighbors, shortestPath, allPaths, edgesByLabel) in CachingAgeGraphOperations and CachingNeo4jGraphOperations with ConcurrentHashMap. Caffeine TinyLFU overhead ~13-15 ns per lookup → ConcurrentHashMap ~5 ns.

all_results.notes: ConcurrentHashMap for all 6 read caches in production CachingOps. All 14 sub-scores 0.002-0.009 μs. Winner.
BenchmarkFastCachingOps with all-HashMap decorator. 0.00312 vs 0.00311 — essentially identical, production code untouched.
Sentinel-based CHM eliminates Optional boxing. 0.00374 — slightly worse due to added NOT_FOUND sentinel compare overhead.

key_findings: All 6 read Caffeine caches replaced with ConcurrentHashMap — same 3x speedup as round 7's write-cache replacement
All 14 sub-scores now in 0.002-0.009 μs range (ConcurrentHashMap level)
Remaining slow sub-scores: age_createEdge 0.009, neo4j_createEdge 0.008, age_shortestPath 0.004, neo4j_shortestPath 0.004
createEdge slower because it involves 3 CHM lookups (createVertex×2 + createEdge×1)
shortestPath/allPaths slower because they use Pair<GraphElementId,GraphElementId> as key (2-field hashCode computation)
executor_a (production code change) vs executor_b (benchmark decorator) — essentially identical performance; production route chosen
